result:
A component re-renders when its state changes, its parent re-renders, or a context it reads changes. Before fixing anything, open the React DevTools Profiler and enable "Record why each component rendered": re-renders are usually cheap, so only fix the ones that are measurably slow.

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Parent re-rendered.** Children re-render by default, even with identical props. | Wrap the child in `React.memo`, or pass the expensive subtree as `children` so the parent's state change doesn't recreate it. |
| **State lives too high.** An input's state in a page-level component re-renders the whole page on each keystroke. | Move the state down into the smallest component that uses it. |
| **New prop references every render.** Inline `{}`, `[]` and `() => {}` props defeat `React.memo`. | Hoist constants out of the component, and use `useMemo`/`useCallback` for the rest. React Compiler does this automatically if you can enable it. |
| **Context value changes.** `value={{ user, setUser }}` is a new object each render, so every consumer re-renders. | Memoize the value with `useMemo`, and split contexts that change at different rates (for example state and dispatch). |
| **State set to a new but equal object.** React only skips the update when `Object.is` says the value is the same. | Return the previous reference when nothing changed, or store primitives. |
| **Derived state synced in an effect.** `useEffect(() => setFiltered(...), [items])` causes an extra render every time. | Compute it during render: `const filtered = items.filter(...)`, with `useMemo` only if it is expensive. |
| **Store selector returns a new object.** `useSelector(s => ({ a: s.a, b: s.b }))` looks changed on every store update. | Select primitives separately, or use `shallowEqual` (Redux) or `useShallow` (Zustand). |
| **A hook subscribes to more than you need.** Router, form and query hooks can re-render you on any change. | Use the library's narrower selector hook, or move the hook call into a smaller child component. |
| **Component defined inside another component.** It gets a new identity each render, so it remounts and loses state. | Define it at module level. |
| **Unstable keys.** `key={Math.random()}` remounts every item, and index keys do the same on reordered lists. | Use a stable ID from the data. |
| **StrictMode in development.** It deliberately renders twice. | Nothing to fix; it does not happen in production. |

Try the structural fixes first (moving state down, passing `children`, deriving values during render). They remove the re-render at its source, whereas `memo`, `useMemo` and `useCallback` silently stop working as soon as one prop reference is unstable.
